class.name: ParticipantWindow
class.brief_description: An isolated window and viewport tree for one local participant.
class.description: Several participants sharing one process each need their own viewport, their own world and their own input, and a [Window] is the only node that gives all three. This is that window plus the identity of the participant mounted in it: [member mounted_tree], [member peer_id] and [member username] say whose it is, and [method ParticipantViewport.add_slot] places it. A window arrives hidden and borderless, so a process that never asks for a display never opens one. Only a tiler or an author calling [method set_tiled_rect] makes it visible. [codeblock] var slot := ParticipantWindow.new() slot.own_world_3d = true slot.world_3d = World3D.new() slot.username = &"player_two" add_child(slot) tiler.add_slot(slot) tiler.assign_device(1, slot) [/codeblock] The [code]stretch_[/code] knobs are [ParticipantView]'s, resolved the same way against the project's [code]display/window/stretch/*[/code] settings, and land on this window's own [member Window.content_scale_mode] family. A child [Window] inherits none of the root's content scaling on its own, so without this a tiled participant would draw at raw pixel size while the root window scaled. [method send_input] is the routed path a container uses to deliver an event this window did not receive itself, such as a joypad bound to a particular seat. Events queue and flush deferred rather than being pushed where they arrive, because pushing input from inside an input callback re-enters the tree the caller is still walking.

method.name: send_input
method.description: Queues [param event] for this window's viewport, flushed as a local event on the next deferred pass. The routed path: use it when something outside this window decided the event belongs to it. Events this window receives through normal focus need no help.

method.name: set_tiled_rect
method.description: Places this window at [param rect] and re-resolves its content scaling for the new size. What [ParticipantViewport] calls on every slot when the tiling changes.

members.member: The session tree mounted inside this window. Identity rather than machinery: nothing here reads it, and it is how a caller holding a window finds the participant's session. Answers [code]null[/code] once that tree is freed.
The network peer id assigned to the participant in this window. Zero until the participant has joined.
How the design resolution is fitted into this window, resolved onto [member Window.content_scale_aspect]. Inherits the project's answer by default.
The logical resolution this window's contents draw at, resolved onto [member Window.content_scale_size]. [code]Vector2i(0, 0)[/code] inherits the project's viewport size.
Which end of the fit this window renders at, resolved onto [member Window.content_scale_mode]. Inherits the project's answer by default.
Divides the design resolution, resolved onto [member Window.content_scale_factor]. Zero or less inherits the project's answer.
Whether the fit may land on a fractional multiple of the design, resolved onto [member Window.content_scale_stretch]. Inherits the project's answer by default.
The name the participant in this window joined under. Identity, like [member peer_id], and the readable half of it.
